about: NHLPA '93 (SNES) instruments <-> General MIDI. The game has no instrument names, so every row is a guess from the samples (measured length, loop, harmonics, noisiness) and from how the songs use them; nothing was auditioned. Edit by ear. Notes use MIDI = note index + 12 for every instrument (docs/NHL93S-SOUND.md).

0.why: 197 ms pluck, strongly periodic, played G#0-F2: electric bass (finger)

1.why: 124 ms low thump at one fixed key, 1027 uses on the drum parts: kick

2.why: 239 ms bright burst at one fixed key, 574 uses: snare

4.why: 377 ms decaying pluck, played F1-D#3: synth bass 1

5.why: 43 ms bright tick at one fixed key, 900 uses: closed hi-hat

7.why: 112-sample loop with an attack part, strong second harmonic, the main melodic voice of the organ songs: rock organ

8.why: 125 ms noise burst (zero crossings near 7 kHz), 50 uses: crash cymbal

10.why: pure sine loop: the whistle effect: whistle

11.why: 845 ms noise swell, the crowd cheer: applause

27.why: 160-sample loop with strong 3rd, 4th and 8th harmonics, the lead of all four fanfares: synth brass 1

28.why: 112 ms noise burst at keys 13-23, the fanfares' drum part: hand clap
